newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil posts 167 mln reais April budget surplus.
newsitem.headline: Brazil posts 167 mln reais April budget surplus.

text.p: Brazil's Treasury said it posted an operational budget surplus of 167 million reais in the month of April.

The Treasury said April's figure reduced the January-April operational deficit, which includes debt servicing costs, to an equivalent of 0.2 percent of gross domestic product, down from 0.55 percent of GDP in the same period last year.
During April, federal receipts totalled 9.598 billion reais and non-debt expenses 8.168 billion reais, giving the Treasury a primary surplus, which does not include debt costs, of 1.43 billion reais.
Debt serving costs during the month totalled 1.263 billion reais, the Treasury said in a statement.
In April 1996, Brazil posted an operational deficit of 1.275 billion reais and a primary deficit of 826 million reais, the statement said.
The operational deficit in the first four months of 1997 totalled 549 million reais, down from 1.419 billion reais in the same period last year.
The January-April primary surplus in 1997 stood at 3.438 billion reais, or 1.27 percent of GDP, compared with a surplus of 1.989 billion reais, or 0.78 percent of GDP, last year.

The Treasury said its nominal deficit, which includes interest payments and adjusts for foreign exchange fluctuations, was 552 million reais in April and 5.137 billion reais, or 1.90 percent of GDP, in the first four months of the year.
The nominal deficit was 2.580 billion reais in April 1996 and 5.089 billion reais, or 1.99 percent of GDP, in the first four months of last year, the statement said.
The Treasury statement said federal receipts in April were 23.4 percent higher than in April last year and 2.3 percent up from March, the main factor behind the improved performance during the month.

The statment also cited lower spending on payrolls which was 3.6 percent lower in April than in the same month last year. During the first four months of the year, payroll costs were 7.1 percent lower than in the January-April period of 1996.
The Treasury also said its net debt stood at 120.8 billion reais in April. Of that total, 57.1 billion reais was in foreign debt.
